prospect.name: Damien
prospect.aka: Surname never stated. The Zoom display label is the device name 'Samsung SM-A366U'; the rep addresses him as Damien and once as Damian.
prospect.occupation: Paid caregiver for his mother through the state, via a union. Starting two businesses: a vending operation at music and town festivals, and a mobile mechanic business. Self-described as 'a starving businessman right now.'
prospect.family_status: Ex-partner of seven years left about a year ago. One brother died by suicide; his father divorced his mother and withdrew after a workplace injury and a decade on prescribed opioids; he has not spoken to aunts, uncles or cousins in over a decade; his younger brother spat in his face a few weeks before the call. His mother, whom he cares for, is the only blood family in his life, plus an occasional niece. Describes himself as having no community and no purpose.
prospect.training_background: Wrestled through school and describes years of it. Down from 265 lb to 223 lb over about a year with no formal training programme — instead deliberate daily movement, refusing the lift to his third-floor apartment, slow controlled carrying of toolboxes. Has done push-ups, sit-ups and squats with his ex until an umbilical hernia stopped him. No current structured training; the rep never asked what he does now.
prospect.medical: Ankylosing spondylitis, described by the prospect as 'my immune system is attacking my spinal column and fusing it together', with doctors having told him that if he stops moving he is finished. Takes about an hour each morning to get his back mobile enough to get out of bed. Umbilical hernia that visibly protrudes and causes pain during sit-ups; his doctor said there was nothing to be done but lose weight. Two shoulder surgeries following chronic dislocations. Raised cholesterol and triglycerides. Gets winded very easily. Schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type, plus ADHD — months of mania followed by two to three weeks of severe depression. In recovery from drug addiction. Was previously in the process of applying for disability. None of this was asked for; every item was volunteered.

signals: Explicitly reclaiming a former self: 'I want to regain control of my life', 'I need to take my life back', and a target of 'some semblance of a wrestling physique'.
Lost ground across a single hard season — a seven-year relationship ended, addiction and recovery, a brother's suicide, a father's decline, and a near-miss with permanent disability.
Has already clawed back 42 lb unaided and stalled: 'I've kind of been stuck fluctuating there for a while now.'
Visible regret and self-assessment: 'I don't feel accomplished. I don't feel like I have purpose', and 'I'm a balding middle-aged man that looks eight months pregnant.'

the_prehab_fighter was considered — ankylosing spondylitis is active and he is training partly to fight it — but the dominant narrative is recovery from a collapsed period rather than a single acute health event.

objections.raw_quote: So I I don't have that. I'm trying to figure out a way to get that. Let's I, I might be able to take out a loan.
objections.rep_response: Ran the open-wallet play in full — isolation, the should-versus-how reframe, the permission question, then income, expenses, monthly surplus, credit score and available credit. The numbers came back as $2,500 a month income, roughly $300 left over, and $300 of total credit. The rep then offered a $600-700 per month third-party finance option he acknowledged the prospect probably would not qualify for, and an in-house plan of '$1,200 a month over six months', asked about the credit union loan, and set a weekly follow-up cadence.

objections.raw_quote: Worst case scenario, I'm going to start stacking some money away.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it and confirmed the weekly contact: 'Perfect, dude. Okay. We're always here. I'm a text away.'

offer.payment_plan_terms: Two routes were described. Third-party financing: 'you need probably a little bit of a higher credit score for it... like usually kind of 700... it would still usually be, you know, we're still looking at six, 700 bucks a month.' In-house: 'we can break it up into six, but we add a little bit of interest. So it's 1200 a month over six months is what it looks like.' The in-house total of $7,200 against the $6,000 headline was never stated, and the interest was described only as 'a little bit'. Both options exceed the prospect's disclosed $300 monthly surplus by a factor of two to four. The rep also offered to improvise further: 'I'm happy to do some weird custom thing if we need to.'

prospect_financials.note: Income about $2,500 a month. Rent $1,300, food about $400, insurance $57, no car payment. Roughly $300 left at month end, less when petrol or vehicle repairs intervene. Credit score fell from 737 to about 675 on opening a new line. Total credit available: one $300 line plus a secured card of about $150 which is his own money. Netflix already cancelled to stabilise finances; working with recovery programmes and credit unions on debt.

evidence: No payment, no agreement and no deposit. On hearing $6,000 the prospect said 'So I I don't have that.'
Intent was as high as it gets — asked to rate the programme one to ten with finances aside he answered '10', and confirmed the all-in commitment question with 'Yes.'

An explicit ongoing follow-up was agreed, with the rep giving his personal number: 'I'll ping you, like, once a week just to see where things are at' and 'let me know what you find out one way or another, and then we can figure out some next steps from there.'
The prospect's stated next actions were to ask his credit union about a loan and otherwise to 'start stacking some money away'.

COUNTER-EVIDENCE: the financial picture taken on the call makes both offered payment routes unaffordable on the prospect's own numbers, so this follow-up has no path to a sale that does not involve borrowing.
outcome.next_step: Prospect to approach his credit union about a personal loan and to try to save; rep to text weekly. No date set and no product change on the table.

notable.note: The most serious call in the batch on every axis. Clinically: ankylosing spondylitis actively fusing the spine, an untreated umbilical hernia that protrudes under abdominal load, two reconstructed shoulders, raised lipids and schizoaffective disorder were all disclosed, every one of them volunteered — the rep never asked a single health or injury question. He then pitched loaded kettlebell training, told the prospect the mobility work would help 'the autoimmune stuff going on', prescribed 'a pound of meat and six eggs a day' to a man who had just disclosed raised cholesterol and triglycerides, and suggested that people with serious depression come out of the programme saying 'I'm not depressed anymore'. Commercially: the open-wallet play was run properly and returned $2,500 a month income, $300 of monthly surplus and $300 of available credit, after which the prospect was offered a $1,200 a month in-house plan and a $600-700 a month finance option, asked about a credit union loan, and put on a weekly contact cadence. And immediately before the price, the rep asked why community mattered so much and received an account of a brother's suicide, an estranged family and total isolation; the next thing said was 'Here's what I'm going to do... I'll run you through the investment.'
